result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.contract_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Contract two nodes by merging v into u. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11663-L11768){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.contract_nodes( u, v, self_loops=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Creates a new graph where node `v` is removed and all its edges are redirected to node `u`. If there was an edge between `u` and `v`, it becomes a self-loop on `u` (unless `self_loops=False`). This operation does not modify the original graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [u]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to keep (node ID or label). All edges from `v` will be redirected here. [v]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to merge into `u` (node ID or label). This node will be removed. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between `u` and `v` become self-loops on `u`. If `False`, such edges are removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `v` contracted into `u`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `u` and `v` are the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(E)` where `E` is the number of edges - creates a new graph; original is unchanged - node `u` retains its label and attributes - edge weights are preserved - for multigraphs, duplicate edges may be removed ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#c272a799 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a path: A -- B -- C -- D g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) result = g.contract_nodes("A", "B") result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: "B" is gone entirely -- its connections were redirected to "A" instead: ::: {#56b6b9a6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.has_node("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: When the two merged nodes were already connected to each other, that edge becomes a self-loop on the surviving node -- unless `self_loops=False` removes it instead: ::: {#237757fa .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) with_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=True) without_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=False) with_loop.count_all_loops(), without_loop.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, 0) ``` ::: ::: This makes contraction a convenient way to simplify a graph by merging nodes that should be treated as one -- for example, collapsing two adjacent nodes of a path: ::: {#4becb72d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(5) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 simplified = g.contract_nodes(2, 3) simplified.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
